Topic 3.1: Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and vocabulary, part of Transport Suggested vocabulary fly, float, road, rail, water, air, tarmac, fast, in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Why should we listen attentively when other people are talking?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to an oral text featuring the target letter- sound combinations, o/s/ as in dress, o/l/- call, tall o‘fl’ as in flew o/ eɪ / as in way, grey

2. say words with the target letter-sound combinations.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to an oral text featuring the target letter- sound combinations, o/s/ as in dress, o/l/- call, tall o‘fl’ as in flew o/ eɪ / as in way, grey
2. say words with the target letter-sound combinations.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication as the learner listens attentively and responds appropriately to two-directional instructions.

● Learning to learn; the learner’s ability to learn independently is enriched as they practice saying words with the target letter-sound combinations

correctly.

Values:
Respect; acceptance is achieved as the learner understands and appreciates others during group discussions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills; the learner’ self-esteem is nurtured as they are able to read words with the target letter sound combinations correctly.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner applies attentive listening skills in learning of concepts in other learning areas
